walkthroughs.body_html:
Distance-time graphs show how far you've travelled over time.

Flat line = stationary.
Slanted straight line = constant speed.
Steeper slope = faster.
Curve getting steeper = accelerating.

The gradient of a distance-time graph = the speed!

A typical school journey graph might show:

1. Slanted line - walking to bus stop.
2. Flat line - waiting for bus.
3. Steep slanted line - bus is fast.
4. Flat line again - at school.

Reading graphs tells the whole story without words.

To change m/s into km/h: multiply by 3.6.

Example: 10 m/s × 3.6 = 36 km/h.

To go the other way (km/h to m/s): divide by 3.6.

Example: 72 km/h ÷ 3.6 = 20 m/s.
